Geological Field Methods for Geophysicists (1) This course is intended for precandidacy geophysics students who have little practical geological experience. We will learn to use: Brunton compasses, GPS, topographic and geological maps and airphotos, and proper note-taking habits. We will explore the geology of Fossil Canyon (near Ocotillo), learn to determine age relationships and how to read the rock record for clues about the geological history of the area, including the opening of the Gulf of California. Prerequisites: graduate standing or consent of instructor. SIOG 242. Rates and Dates: Applications of Modern Geochronology Methods

Shifting Ideologies of Gender and Sexuality in Science (4) Explore how contemporary understandings of gender and sexuality have been influenced by research in science and medicine and how preconceptions about gender and sexuality influence research. How are discrepancies between what scientists assume about gender and sexual difference reconciled with evidence to the contrary? How have ideas changed over time? Topics range from sex differences in health outcomes, intersexuality, neuroplasticity, environmental exposure, and sports medicine. Prerequisites: upper-division standing. SOCI 171.
